_readme: Linux root filesystem images drac-Xterm can download, keyed by Android ABI.
The app reads Build.SUPPORTED_ABIS first and only shows the entries under a
matching key. Only arm64-v8a is listed, because that is the only ABI the
bundled proot/busybox binaries are built for (abiFilters in app/build.gradle.kts).
Adding another ABI here means building its binaries first, or the download
succeeds and nothing in it can run.
Every entry carries a sha256. RootfsDownloader refuses to hand an archive to
the extractor unless the digest of the completed file matches exactly. An
entry without a valid 64-hex digest is dropped when this file is parsed.
Two kinds of source appear here, and the difference matters:
* kali.download. Kali publishes both the image and SHA256SUMS, so those three
digests can be re-derived from the project itself.
* images.linuxcontainers.org. Where the Debian image comes from. It publishes
SHA256SUMS next to every build and a detached OpenPGP signature for both the
tarball and that sums file, so the pin below can be re-derived from an
independent authority -- something the previous Debian source could not offer.
It replaced easycli.sh, which hosted the Debian image until its operator
disabled hosting for good: the URL now answers 302 -> / with a 43-byte notice,
and the SHA-256 pin correctly refused to install it. That failure is the reason
this entry moved.
One caveat, and it is the reason a self-hosted mirror is still wanted: the
image server keeps only about three days of dated builds, so the URL below
stops resolving once this build rotates out. Re-point it at a mirror you
control (the digest stays valid wherever the same bytes are served).
